questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was close to my home country, and I like the nature around Bergen. Furthermore, UiB had some courses which is well aligned with my education at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine. I used some time, but it is expected when you are going to study abroad.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much physically, but I have written to the information centers and got the help I needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I luckily knew someone living in Bergen, who could help me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: People should know that you need to put much effort into get to know people. People living at for instance Fantoft will automatically meet other students daily, so if you would like the certainty of get to know people, it would be the better choice. I really liked living in the city and the freedom coming from that, so I really recommend living off campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not have much to comment on, it was fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Fine online support.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Believe that it will be fine in the end, you will experience a lot of confusion, but I will be solved during time if you put some time in it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the course materials very good. I could have wished for more attendance and work together with co-students, but the courses were interesting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I do prefer the way they do it in Copenhagen. In Copenhagen we have a lot of classes during a week and really good opportunities to get to know other students at the course. As an exchange student I would have wished it was the same in Bergen. In general we could attend to classes 6 hours a week, and I found it unsatisfied.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environmental Psychology
Climate Policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Them both if you are interested in political systems and individuals ability and current way of addressing climate change and environmental problems.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Studentsamfundet facilitates some interesting debates every Tuesday morning I enjoyed. But in generally the host institution have not played a big role in my daily life here in Bergen.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found a football team which was not a part of the university. I liked meeting some people who was not Erasmus and lived in Bergen.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go discover the area around Bergen. So many good places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy since I do live in Scandinavia in general.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask what they like to do and for some good tips, then they will be more likely to invite you or show you some nice things.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Norwegians are (like danes) not the most open people and it can be difficult to get to know people. But people do like to help others, you just have to reach out more than you are used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are polite and very sweet. I have not had any bad experiences with the culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to be a part of an association - it a nice way to meet others. 
Find peace in having a more relaxing daily life than in Copenhagen. I have enjoyed having more time to study and go for a hike.
Third thing: GO! Bergen is a really nice city with opportunities for nature experiences and a nice modern city with nice bars, cinemas and concerts.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The studies and to live a more peaceful life for 6 months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To socialize. But if you put some effort in it in the beginning, you will enjoy it for the last part of your stay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
